newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JUNEAU AND BONDRA LEAD CAPS PAST SLUMPING LEAFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-JUNEAU AND BONDRA LEAD CAPS PAST SLUMPING LEAFS.

text.p: Joe Juneau had two goals and an assist and Peter Bondra continued his torrid scoring pace with a pair of goals as the Washington Capitals doubled up the struggling Toronto Maple Leafs 6-3 on Monday.
Juneau and Bondra scored 1:47 apart in the second period as the Capitals built a 4-1 advantage.
Bondra has 12 goals and two assists during a 10-game scoring streak for Washington, which is 4-0-2 in the new year.
Mats Sundin had a pair of assists for the Maple Leafs, who suffered their fifth straight loss to fall in into a tie for last place overall in the NHL with 34 points.
Kelly Miller and Andrei Nikolishin scored first-period goals for the Capitals, while Sergei Berezin and Jirk Muller had powerplay goals for the Leafs.
Washington goaltender Jim Carey made 27 saves.
Bondra's second goal of the game, a short-handed tally, was his 27th of the season.
"He's legitimate," said Capitals coach Jim Schoenfeld.

"In the lockout season he led the league in goal scoring and there were some doubters who said he wouldn't be able to maintain it over the course of (a full) season. Peter is a bonafide National Hockey League goal scorer."

In Chicago, Rick Tabaracci made 27 saves for his 10th career shutout and John Cullen and Rob Zamuner scored as the Tampa Bay Lightning extended their unbeaten streak to five games with a 2-0 blanking of the Blackhawks.
It was Tabaracci's second shutout of the season and first since coming to Tampa Bay from Calgary. He is 5-0-3 in his last eight decisions.
Cullen gave Tabaracci all the offence he needed with 3:06 left in the first when he blasted a slap shot from the right point past Jeff Hackett's stick side.
In Boston, Alexandre Daigle's goal with 82 seconds left in the third period lifted the Ottawa Senators to their first-ever win in Boston, a 4-3 victory over the Bruins.
Adam Oates scored his 14th goal with 4:30 left in the third period to boost Boston into a 3-3 tie. But Daigle scored the game-winner just over three minutes later.
Boston goalie Tim Cheveldae got a piece of a shot by Shaun Van Allen, but the rebound rolled to his right and Daigle flipped the puck between Cheveldae and the far post.
Christer Olsson had a goal and an assist for the Senators, who had lost in all 11 of their previous visits to Boston.

In Montreal, Jamie Langenbrunner's powerplay goal with 3:54 left in the second period broke a tie and Andy Moog made 16 saves as the Dallas Stars edged the Canadiens 2-1 for their first win in Montreal in nearly a decade.
Jere Lehtinen had the other goal for Dallas, which had been 0-8-2 at Montreal since winning at the old Forum on February 23, 1987.
Turner Stevenson scored the lone Montreal goal and Andy Moog made 31 saves for the Habs as the Stars outshot the Canadiens 33-17.
In New York, Zigmund Palffy and Brent Hughes scored 14 seconds apart in the first period as the New York Islanders broke a seven-game winless streak by holding on for a 4-2 victory over the Rangers.
Travis Green and Scott Lachance added powerplay goals for the Islanders, who always seem to play their best against their local rivals, the Rangers.
Tommy Salo made 28 saves, including a pair of stellar stops on Wayne Gretzky in the second period.
Brian Leetch and Luc Robitaille tallied for the Rangers after spotting the Isles a 3-0 lead.
In San Jose, Tony Granato's second goal of the game with 48 seconds remaining in regulation gave the Sharks a 5-4 win over the Phoenix Coyotes.
Granato snapped a 4-4 tie. He took a cross-ice pass from Bernie Nicholls and lifted the puck over goaltender Nikolai Khabibulin and just under the crossbar for the game-winner.

Nicholls had three assists, including the 700th of his career. Keith Tkachuk had a pair of goals and Cliff Ronning added a goal and two assists for Phoenix, which has dropped five of its last six games.
